title: How OEMs Reduce Wire Complexity with Distributed J1939 I/O Modules
summary: Learn how OEMs cut wire complexity, reduce weight, and save money using distributed J1939 I/O modules in heavy-duty vehicles.
body_markdown:
As mobile equipment becomes more advanced across heavy-duty vehicles and equipment, OEMs often need to manage more sensors, switches, actuators, operator controls and electronic functions across the vehicle. This can lead to larger wiring harnesses, longer wire runs, higher material costs and more complex installation and service requirements.


This article will explain how distributed J1939 I/O modules help reduce wringing complexity in heavy duty vehicles. By replacing heavy, centralized wiring harnesses with decentralized node, the J1939 I.O module offers simplified vehicle design.


### How J1939 I/O Modules Works


This device ensures a smooth control, process and connection in an industrial network. It includes 4 digital inputs, 2 sourcing outputs, 1 sinking output and 13A max total module current. Making it a compact device that is IP67 and can be used in 12V and 24V nominal systems. This expansion module us built in short circuit and overload protection along with reverse battery and over-voltage protection on the module.


### Key Benefits


Original equipment manufacturers use distributed J1939 input/output modules to replace massive, centralized wiring harnesses with a simple, shared serial communication network. These are some of the benefits of using distributed J1939 I/O modules in OEMs.


**Reduced Wiring:** Eliminates individual wires that need to stretch long into the main control area and reduces overall vehicle weight and material cost.


**Multiplexed Communication** : Lightweight and handles efficient data transmission.


**Easier System Expansion:** By using a shared standardized CAN bus network, it allows multiple electronic control units to function seamlessly.


**Serviceability and Lower Installation Cost:** Simple harness that takes less time and money with easier repairs.


### Frequently Asked Questions


Why is wiring complexity increasing in modern mobile equipment


The added sensors, actuators, controls, electronic functions, and configuration options can make wiring harnesses larger, heavier, more expensive, and harder to install or maintain.


What are distributed J1939 I/O Modules?


CAN-connected input/output devices that allow OEMs to place signal collection and output control closer to sensors, switches, actuators, and other equipment components
